summary: Zimbabwe's Department of Immigration sorts nationalities into categories: Category A, including South Africa and Botswana, does not require a visa; Category B, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, requires a visa that may be obtained at the port of entry after paying the fee (its fee schedule lists USD 30 for an ordinary single entry at the port of entry); and the eVisa portal says nationals of a third list must pay for and obtain a visa before travelling.

safety.text: The UK government says there is a moderate level of crime: mugging, pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in city centres, especially after dark, and there have been smash-and-grab robberies from vehicles. It says there is a shortage of physical US dollar cash, that there are frequent power blackouts, that demonstrations and rallies may turn violent and political gatherings should be avoided, and to stop at roadblocks and get a receipt if you have to pay a fine.

tips.text: The UK government says the KAZA Univisa (USD 50) is valid for 30 days for travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia and for day trips into Botswana, and is sold at Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls airports and at the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders.

The UK government says there is a shortage of physical US dollar cash, so it is not always possible to make withdrawals using an international debit or credit card, and that change is rarely available, so carry small denomination notes.

Zimbabwe's eVisa portal sorts nationalities into lists: visitors from the first are not required to have a visa, visitors from the second will pay for and obtain a visa upon entering Zimbabwe, and visitors from the third must pay for and obtain a visa before travelling.

The UK government says it is illegal to photograph government offices, airports, military establishments, political party offices, official residences, embassies and other sensitive locations without special permission from the Ministry of Information, and illegal to photograph police and armed forces personnel, demonstrations and protests. Canada's travel advice says it is illegal for civilians to wear any form of clothing made from camouflage material.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: Zimbabwe's Department of Immigration says Category B nationalities, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, require a visa that may also be obtained at the port of entry after paying the fee, though it encourages processing the visa online before travelling; its fee schedule lists USD 30 for an ordinary single entry. Category A nationalities, including South Africa and Botswana, do not require a visa, while the eVisa portal says nationals of a third list must pay for and obtain a visa before travelling.

faq.question: How much is the Zimbabwe visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The Department of Immigration's fee schedule lists USD 30 for an ordinary single entry at the port of entry, and online rates of USD 30 for an ordinary single entry, USD 55 single and USD 70 double entry for British citizens and USD 60 single entry for Chinese citizens, plus USD 55 for a multiple-entry visa. The UK government advises taking enough US dollars in small notes to pay for the visa.

faq.question: What is the KAZA UniVisa?
faq.answer: The UK government says the KAZA Univisa costs USD 50, is valid for 30 days for travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia and for day trips into Botswana, and is available at Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls airports and at the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders. Zimbabwe's eVisa portal describes it as a special visa allowing entry into multiple countries within the Kavango Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area within one month.

faq.question: What currency should I bring to Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: The UK government says Zimbabwe has a multi-currency system and you can use US dollars for most transactions; it says Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) was introduced in April 2024 to replace the Zimbabwean dollar and the US dollar remains legal tender, and that change is rarely available, so carry small denomination notes.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: The UK government says the visa on arrival is usually granted for 30 days and that to extend or renew a visa you go in person to the Government of Zimbabwe Immigration Department. No official source we could read states the length of an extension.
